summary: Provision contextual Slack thread archiver that auto-creates Jira runbooks and performs on-the-fly translation
description: Request: Build a Slack automation that watches designated channels, snapshots long/important threads to Confluence as lightweight runbooks, optionally spins up a linked internal Jira ticket when the thread contains action items (detect via simple heuristics), and performs on-the-fly translation for non-English threads. Rationale: We have recurring support and post-incident threads that live in Slack and get lost; engineering and SRE teams want a low-friction way to capture actions and runbooks without manual copy/paste. This should reduce knowledge loss, speed incident follow-ups, and satisfy retention/compliance needs. Constraints: minimal latency impact to Slack UX, strictly respect channel-level RBAC and privacy flags, and provide admins an allowlist of channels and a per-channel retention tag. Privacy note: translation and content extraction must obey existing data classification rules (sensitive content must not be auto-exported).
request_steps: 1) Product/ops owner identifies channels to opt-in. 2) Install Slack app with event subscriptions and message:read scope under org bot token. 3) Configure Confluence page template and Jira project mapping in a small JSON config stored in Vault. 4) Enable translation pipeline (on-demand) using existing translate service; translation only runs when thread contains non-en-US locale header or user flag. 5) Provide admin UI + audit logs in Confluence page and a /archive-thread slash command for manual snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can add/remove channels to the archiver allowlist via an internal UI or config file
When enabled, long threads (>8 messages) are summarized and exported to a Confluence runbook page using the runbook template
If action-detection heuristics match (TODO:, ACTION:, follow-up), the automation creates a Jira ticket pre-populated with title, summary, and a link to the Confluence runbook
Exports are labeled with a retention tag and are visible in the Confluence audit log
Translation runs only when a thread is detected as non-English or a user requests translation via slash command
RBAC: automation respects private channel membership; messages from users outside the channel are excluded from exports
Rate-limited to avoid hitting Slack API quotas; configurable throttle settings present in config

Slack scopes required: channels:history, groups:history, im:history, mpim:history, chat:write, users:read, admin.conversations:read (for org-level ops). Security flagged admin scopes as high-risk.
Translation: prototype using translate-service v2 yields acceptable accuracy for EU languages; latency observed ~150-300ms per chunk (needs batching).
